title: Albert Wendt, “Towards a New Oceania”
place: Suva, Fiji (University of the South Pacific)
note: Introduction to the inaugural issue of Mana Review, USP's literary journal; a founding text for the idea of a new Oceania.

title: The Contemporary Pacific begins publication
place: Honolulu, Hawaiʻi (Center for Pacific Islands Studies, UH Mānoa)
note: Founded at the UH Center for Pacific Islands Studies; later the home of Hauʻofa (1994), Gegeo & Watson-Gegeo, Meyer (2001), Thaman (2003) and Kaʻili (2005).

title: A New Oceania: Rediscovering Our Sea of Islands
place: Suva, Fiji (USP School of Social and Economic Development)
note: Waddell, Naidu & Hauʻofa (eds), a USP 25th-anniversary volume opening with Hauʻofa’s “Our Sea of Islands” and essays responding to it.

title: Decolonizing Methodologies published
place: Dunedin, Aotearoa (University of Otago Press) and London (Zed Books)
note: Linda Tuhiwai Smith’s book, the most cited text in this corpus’s genealogy.

title: Rethinking Pacific Education idea formed
note: Konai Helu Thaman, Ana Taufeʻulungaki, Kabini Sanga and NZAID discuss Pacific educators meeting without donors to rethink education from Pacific perspectives.

title: First RPEIPP colloquium
note: Rethinking Pacific Education Initiative for and by Pacific Peoples; hosted by USP’s Institute of Education with Victoria University of Wellington. Recommendations went to Forum Education Ministers in May 2001.

title: Pasifika Education Research Guidelines
place: Auckland, Aotearoa (for the Ministry of Education)
note: Anae, Coxon, Mara, Wendt-Samu & Finau; a final report to the Ministry of Education. Not in OpenAlex.

title: HRC Guidelines on Pacific Health Research
note: Written to guide HRC-funded research with Pacific peoples.

title: RPEIPP moves to USP’s Institute of Education
note: Led by Victoria University of Wellington 2001–2004, the initiative moves to USP in 2005.

title: HRC Pacific Health Research Guidelines (revised)
note: Revision building on the 2005 guidelines; covers Aotearoa and the realm countries (Cook Islands, Niue, Tokelau). Not in OpenAlex.

title: Forum leaders endorse the Blue Pacific narrative
note: Theme: “The Blue Pacific – Our Sea of Islands – Our Security Through Sustainable Development, Management and Conservation”.

title: Talanoa Dialogue at COP23 (Fiji presidency)
note: The Fijian presidency announces the Talanoa Dialogue, carrying talanoa into global climate diplomacy.

title: 2050 Strategy for the Blue Pacific Continent
note: Endorsed by Forum leaders; research and technology is one of its pathways.

title: Blue Pacific Horizons Signature Research Area launched
place: Auckland, Aotearoa (Waipapa Taumata Rau, University of Auckland)
note: Mā Kiwa te moana nui e whakaumu: “Building resilient, just and sustainable futures – grounded in the Pacific, relevant to the world.”
